answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a copper-backed stake that is locked for the whole epoch, so creating many fake identities gets expensive fast. A newcomer earns trust only through a willow-like slow growth of verified work: peers attest completed tasks, and reputation accrues gradually rather than being bought. When a sudden gale of new accounts appears, the network raises the stake and delays their rewards until attestation catches up, so floods of fake agents cost more than they can earn.
